I have no sequence-retrieval, genome-alignment, or guide-design tool in this session — no BLAST/Bowtie, no NCBI/Ensembl access, no shell. That matters here, because a *real* gRNA design with off-target scoring requires (a) the genomic sequence of the target window and (b) a genome-wide mismatch search against GRCh38. I cannot do either, so **I will not print 20-nt protospacers or MIT/CFD scores** — any numbers I produced would be invented, which is worse than no answer.

What I can give you, from knowledge, is the locus information and a complete, parameterised protocol you can execute in ~20 minutes to get real, scored guides. Everything below is knowledge-based and flagged where I'm less certain.

## Target locus (verify coordinates before use)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Gene | *CFTR*, NCBI Gene ID **1080**, HGNC:1884 |
| Locus | **7q31.2**, plus strand |
| Span (GRCh38) | ~chr7:117,480,000–117,669,000 (~189 kb, 27 exons) |
| MANE Select transcript | **NM_000492.4** → protein **NP_000483.3** (1480 aa) |
| Ensembl | ENSG00000001626 / ENST00000003084 |
| F508del | **c.1521_1523delCTT**, p.Phe508del, exon 11 (legacy exon 10), **rs113993960** |
| G551D | **c.1652G>A**, p.Gly551Asp, exon 12 (legacy 11), **rs75527207** |

Confidence note: gene ID, transcript, protein, HGNC, rsIDs and exon assignments I'm confident in. The base-level GRCh38 span is from memory and NCBI's current annotation includes an extended 5′ region, so pull the exact interval from the Gene record rather than from me. Do not hand the design tool a coordinate I gave you without checking it.

## Design protocol (this produces the real guides + scores)

**Tool choice — use CRISPOR** (crispor.gi.ucsc.edu). It is the right default because it reports both standard efficiency and off-target scores *and* flags off-targets overlapping exons and known variants. CHOPCHOP is a reasonable second opinion; Benchling is fine if you're already in it.

1. **Input the region, not the sequence.** CRISPOR accepts coordinates — paste e.g. `chr7:<exon11_start-100>-<exon11_end+100>`. Genome: **Homo sapiens – UCSC hg38**. PAM: **20bp-NGG (SpCas9)**. Include ≥100 bp of flanking intron so you don't lose guides whose PAM sits in the splice flank.
2. **For a knockout** (e.g. CFTR-null cell line): target **exon 3 or exon 4** of NM_000492.4. Avoid exon 1 (alternative starts, high GC, reinitiation downstream) and avoid the last two exons (truncated protein may retain partial function). Pick two guides 40–200 bp apart if you want a confirmable deletion band by PCR.
3. **For F508del correction**: a 3-bp deletion cannot be fixed by base editing (ABE/CBE only do transitions). Your options are HDR with ssODN (low efficiency in airway basal cells, ~1–15%) or **prime editing (PE3/PEmax)**, which is the current method of choice for F508del and needs a *pegRNA* + nicking sgRNA, not a plain sgRNA. Design that in **PrimeDesign** or **pegFinder**, not CRISPOR. If you want the plain-Cas9 route anyway, restrict guides to those cutting within ~10 bp of c.1521 so HDR conversion tracts are short.
4. **Rank on these two scores, in this order:**
   - **Off-target: CFD specificity score (Doench 2016) ≥ 80**; reject anything < 50. Additionally reject any guide with a **0-, 1-, or 2-mismatch** off-target anywhere, and any 3-mismatch off-target inside a coding exon or a known oncogene/tumour suppressor.
   - **On-target efficiency: Doench 2016 "Rule Set 2" ≥ 60** (CRISPOR's default), cross-checked against Moreno-Mateos if you're doing IVT sgRNA.
   - Secondary filters: GC 40–70%, no poly-T (≥4 T's, blocks U6 termination), no >4-nt homopolymer, avoid guides whose seed region sits in a *CFTR* pseudo-paralogous or repeat-masked segment.
5. **Carry 3–4 guides forward**, not one. Score-to-activity correlation is modest (r ≈ 0.4–0.5); empirical screening beats prediction.

## Off-target validation beyond in-silico scoring

Computational scores are predictions, not measurements. For anything heading toward therapeutic or publication-grade work:

- **CIRCLE-seq** or **CHANGE-seq** — in-vitro, genome-wide, highest sensitivity, no cells needed. Best first empirical screen.
- **GUIDE-seq** — in-cell, dsODN tag capture; the standard for cell-line work.
- **Targeted amplicon NGS (rhAmpSeq / CRISPResso2)** on the top 20–50 predicted + empirically nominated sites, at ≥10,000× depth to resolve ≥0.1% indel frequency.
- Analyse edits with **CRISPResso2**; report indel spectra, not just "% edited".

## One flag worth raising

If the downstream goal is a CF disease model or a correction experiment, the guide design is the easy part — the limiting factor will be delivery into the relevant cell type (primary human bronchial epithelial cells / organoids are poorly transfectable; RNP electroporation or AAV6 for HDR donor are the usual routes). Worth settling that before locking guide choice, since PAM availability differs between Cas9 and the Cas12a/SpRY variants that some delivery routes favour.

Tell me which objective you want — knockout, F508del correction, or a specific other variant — and I'll write the exact CRISPOR/PrimeDesign input strings and the primer design plan for validation. I still won't be able to run the genome search from this session.

## ANSWER

**UNABLE:** I have no sequence-retrieval or genome-alignment tool in this session, so I cannot generate verified *CFTR* protospacer sequences or compute MIT/CFD off-target scores. Fabricating them would be unacceptable.

Delivered instead, from knowledge: target locus identifiers (*CFTR*, Gene ID **1080**, 7q31.2, MANE **NM_000492.4**, ENSG00000001626; F508del **rs113993960** c.1521_1523delCTT exon 11; G551D **rs75527207**) and an executable design protocol — **CRISPOR** on hg38 with 20bp-NGG, exon 3/4 for knockout, accept **CFD ≥ 80** and **Doench Rule Set 2 ≥ 60**, reject any 0–2-mismatch off-target, carry 3–4 guides, then confirm empirically by **CIRCLE-seq/GUIDE-seq** + targeted amplicon NGS analysed in CRISPResso2. Note: F508del is a 3-bp deletion, so use **prime editing (PrimeDesign/pegFinder)** or HDR, not base editing.
